seo.title: Housing Services | Genesis Garden
seo.description: Genesis Garden provides emergency shelter, eviction prevention, rapid re-housing, and permanent supportive housing in Western Illinois.

hero.heading: Housing Supports & Services
hero.text: Everyone needs a safe and stable place to call home. Home is more than a place — home ignites hope and fuels dreams for healthy people and resilient families.

intro.heading: What Happens Without Housing?
intro.subheading: When there aren't enough safe, stable, and affordable places for everyone to live, the impacts cascade rapidly across every part of life:

impacts.title: Compromised Health
impacts.description: Skipping crucial medications, cutting daily meals, and enduring chronic stress just to make rent.

impacts.title: Doubling Up
impacts.description: Crowding into temporary spaces with relatives or friends under constant instability and uncertainty.

impacts.title: Eviction & Debt
impacts.description: Navigating abrupt legal court notices and rental records that block access to future housing.

impacts.title: Unsheltered Crisis
impacts.description: Displacement into vehicles, temporary motels, or emergency shelters when all options run out.

intro.highlight: But homelessness doesn't have to be hopeless.
intro.paragraph2: If you're struggling with safe, stable housing, you don't have to carry the weight alone. Have a conversation with us — together, we'll listen, advocate, and work toward a solution.

services.heading: Our Solutions
services.subtitle: We offer a range of housing support services tailored to your situation.

items.title: Diversion
items.description: Finding out what it would take for you to stay where you are now. Or re-connecting with family or friends who could house you for at least 30 days.

items.title: Eviction Prevention
items.description: Working with you and/or your landlord, providing financial resources, or referring you to the CBRAP program. In most cases, financial support requires an eviction notice and documentation of means to pay rent going forward.

items.title: Emergency Shelter
items.description: Our primary location, Genesis House, is a large remodeled Victorian era house with private bedrooms and bathrooms, plus shared living, laundry, and kitchen. Leighty House offers similar space. We also use motel rooms when at capacity.

items.title: Rapid Re-Housing
items.description: Financial assistance and support services to move families from no housing into permanent housing as quickly as possible. Support tapers down over several months as the family regains stability.

items.title: Permanent Supportive Housing
items.description: For families with documented long-term disabilities who have lost housing, PSH offers more supportive services and rent subsidies without a specific time limit.

eligibility.heading: Who Can We Help?
eligibility.intro: Most of these options for regaining housing stability are open to:
eligibility.hint: Hover or tap any category to view eligibility details.

items.title: Multi-generational families
items.description: Households bringing grandparents, parents, adult children, and grandchildren together under one roof with shared caregiving and mutual support.

items.title: Single-parent & kinship households
items.description: Solo mothers, solo fathers, legal guardians, and relatives raising children on a single income or navigating caregiver transitions.

items.title: Large & blended families
items.description: Households with multiple dependents, stepfamilies, and extended kin requiring flexible, high-capacity living arrangements.

items.title: Couples & partnerships
items.description: Married spouses, domestic partners, and cohabiting couples (with or without dependents) facing economic hardship or relocation.

items.title: Self-defined & chosen households
items.description: Supportive living arrangements and families formed by mutual bond, shared commitments, or community care rather than legal or biological ties.

items.title: Roommates & shared living groups
items.description: Unrelated adults, students, or peers pooling financial resources to achieve long-term, stable housing affordability.

items.title: Foster & adoptive families
items.description: Families welcoming foster placements, navigating guardianship, or finalizing adoptions who need housing stability during transitional periods.

items.title: Solo adults & independent individuals
items.description: Single adults seeking an affordable home base to establish stability, employment continuity, and personal independence.

items.title: Young adults & aging-out youth
items.description: Unaccompanied young adults (ages 18–24) transitioning out of foster care, educational programs, or temporary youth shelters.

items.title: Returning citizens
items.description: Formerly incarcerated individuals re-entering their communities who need safe, immediate housing to rebuild their foundation.

items.title: Justice-involved applicants
items.description: Individuals with legal records or open proceedings who are routinely locked out of conventional vouchers and traditional housing supports.

items.title: Older adults & fixed-income seniors
items.description: Aging individuals and couples on fixed retirement, SSI, or disability benefits needing accessible, dignified housing.

items.title: Veterans & former service members
items.description: Military veterans and their families seeking civilian stability, emergency housing bridges, or reintegration support.

items.title: Survivors & specialized support needs
items.description: Individuals escaping domestic violence, human trafficking, or those requiring physical accessibility and trauma-informed stability.

otherActivities.heading: Other Activities
otherActivities.title: Summer Meals for Kids
otherActivities.text: Free summer meals for children and youth ages 1–18 at sites across McDonough County, June through mid-August.

cta.heading: Need Housing Help?
cta.text: Call Genesis Garden to talk about your housing needs. We're here to listen and work with you toward a solution.
